PASS-WITH-NOTES — P280-001 acquisition-wait fix accepted; F232 retained as explicitly accepted follow-up.

C34 disposition: pm-001/pij-steady-otter ruled the newly found CodexBinder retry interaction a named FOLLOW-UP, F232, not a round-2 block. It does not convert errors to absence or tombstones; the tmux-server crash fixed here has fleet-wide impact. Silkworm will address F232 in a separate small PR: do not consume the row/lock signal when the pane probe errs. This verdict does not claim the retry gap is fixed. No further review round or hostile-holder hardening is requested.

PR280 / F229 final-round performance review, exact headc8d2eab2fc9e073d8c8b8de27dbb53e8141ec315; delta ONLY fromad27621c0f995aaf4cafcd9937257ebc84018c09. Request01a1f752-a5ae-7ed1-99b7-0a5b2dc36798.

## Original P280-001

The added contention wait is removed. lock_attach (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:496-512) creates/opens the file and performs ONE nonblocking File::try_lock; no sleep or internal retry loop. AttachLockHeld is a distinct inner error (:515-537), so unrelated spawn EAGAIN is not mistaken for lock contention. ask (:337-345) returns Query::Busy until the5s observed-contention boundary; stdout (:469-482) returns an error without launching, and query_live returns None without starting/forking. No state mutex is held across the removed acquisition sleep: it still protects the short acquisition attempt and existing successful attach/setup path.

This closes the ORIGINAL added3s/10ms acquisition-wait defect. It is not a claim that all preexisting synchronous work is gone: successful startup still performs process/pipe/setup and existing3s handshake, live replies still use recv_timeout, and filesystem/mutex operations remain synchronous. Those are unchanged baseline paths, not a new final-round audit.

## Every requested pane-decision consumer

All sources below are under crates/. Err means unknown/error rather than an empty pane inventory or a dead server. Observer, both death witnesses, authoritative revive, registration, close/kill and spawn preserve that separation. Conditional error-to-None mappings require a second successful negative inventory. Explicit owner close is intentionally a different policy from observed-dead reconciliation; spawn.failed is explicitly a failed-unbound request receipt with a live residual, not launch death.

| Consumer | Source | Busy/error decision |
|---|---|---|
| Adapter list/pane process | tmux/src/lib.rs:469-482,881-907,910-925 | Err propagates. Initial pane-process error becomes None only after a SECOND successful inventory proves absence. Live-only unavailable is outer None, not absent. |
| Pane observer | daemon/src/pane_observer.rs:247-265,275-288,356-397 | Global Err records UNKNOWN and exits before retirement; tap/capture errors record unknown and preserve/retry. |
| Death sweep/two witnesses | daemon/src/reaper.rs:65-156,214-245 | Unknown/unverifiable for either failed witness; no observed-dead candidate/tombstone. Never-bound no-live-client remains unknown. |
| Revive | daemon/src/http/revive.rs:323-393,161-199,586-593 | Optional wait's false means stop waiting, not absent. Locked observation records pane_present=None and refuses unless positive Some(false). |
| Registration/adopt/control identity | daemon/src/registration.rs:904-985;http/mod.rs:1157-1162,1332;http/identity.rs:774-843;http/governance.rs:1979-2028 | Pane error propagates Runtime/internal before registration/proof; only successful missing facts become absence/refusal. Holder unknown never enters verified dead-holder tombstones. |
| Owner close/held close | daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:253-287,594-639;http/memory_turn.rs:584-633 | Unknown->Unchecked, no kill advice. Explicit OWNER-authorized retirement is not observed-dead; no automatic kill. CAS retries bounded, not Busy-triggered. |
| Kill/tap deletion/orphan sweep | tmux/src/lib.rs:1382-1395,1447-1508 | Fresh-list await? blocks kill, sink cleanup and absent-set creation on Busy; an already-issued detach write may run, but unavailable evidence retains local sink/state. |
| Spawn | daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1942-2024;spawn_waits.rs:1-23,163-199 | Prelaunch error refuses. Postlaunch error answers failed-UNBOUND/dispatched true while preserving row/pane and parent handoff after later matching binding. No absent/dead conversion. |
| Durable pane delivery/interaction | daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs:253-283,349-365;harnesses/src/interaction.rs:499-568,619-755 | Unknown inventory is None, pane_absent=false; interaction Err preserves queue/retry. Direct delivery restores provisional dedupe on error. |

| Recovery/modal/size observation | daemon/src/auth_recovery.rs:179-223,304-338;modal_stall.rs:45-105;pa_presence.rs:969-1063 | No positive composer/idle proof vetoes action; live-only unknown skips; size failures retain prior size/stale status. No absence/relaunch. |
| Codex spawned-seat binder | daemon/src/codex_bind.rs:143-148,242-265,301,347-352 | Pane error itself propagates, but pending row/lock snapshot were already marked seen. No ordinary same-row/lock retry after release: P280-002 disposition below. |

Additional checks: general whoami/resolve_seat uses roster+liveness, not tmux; normal Copilot statusline therefore does not acquire this lock. Codex caller's held_by_pane propagates Err and only checks identity, it does not bind. Background has no additional direct pane-presence consumer. Cold-wake lack of positive idle evidence suppresses action. No inspected path turns Busy Err directly into pane-absent/server-gone or false observed-dead tombstones. The separate Codex retry suppression below is availability, not a fabricated absence.

## Cost — transient versus frozen holder

Healthy live client:0 added lock-file opens,0flock calls and0added processes per read/tick/seat. One open+try_lock per start/replacement attempt. Instrumentation stays after acquired lock at control.rs:395-406; no new launch site, and unchanged spawn_sites.rs:203-244 still explicitly covers start/run. Existing launches go through resolved program::launch paths.

Busy phase (<5s since first observed contention): each attempted control query does one directory check/create, one lock-file open, one try_lock and returns an allocated typed/error result.0tmux READ launches for that skipped query; writes are unaffected and can still launch. No100Hz retry timer. Observer's failed global inventory returns before all per-pane work, so at default600ms it attempts about1.667lock opens/try_locks per second per affected daemon, not5Nper second (roughly9attempts across a5s Busy interval). Other request-driven consumers contribute their own existing read demand; pane_process can issue two back-to-back queries because it confirms a first error with list_panes. That is bounded disambiguation, not a new unbounded retry loop. Live-only reads perform no acquisition.

Frozen holder: the first query at/after5s becomes Fork, stamps a5s RESTART_BACKOFF and resets contended_since. Reads during backoff fork once per fallback-enabled query, with no lock attempt. After backoff another read starts a new Busy interval if the lock is still held. Therefore indefinite contention is NOT globally launch-free: Busy/fallback intervals repeat, and request arrivals/phase boundaries determine exact totals. Within a fork phase the nominal observer offered demand is D*(1+3N)/0.6 =D*(1.667+5N)launches/s for D affected daemons with N tracked matching-tap panes each; at80panes/one affected daemon,401.667/s, excluding other reads/writes. This is offered cadence demand, not observed throughput or a whole-daemon hard ceiling. Blocking fork cost and missed passes reduce actual averages. Backoff limits START ATTEMPTS, not read forks. No workload-independent total fork-rate cap.

Two healthy processes release the attach flock after the setup sentinel, NOT at client exit, so normal contention is transient and both can become healthy. Release BEFORE failed-start backoff lets the next read attach immediately. Release during an existing frozen-holder backoff still respects that backoff. The5s observation window is demand-driven state, not a new timer; it only advances when reads are attempted.

Cadences remain unchanged: observer600ms; bind/death periodic5s; existing delivery5s plus existing lease wake; revive optional live-only250ms/5s (<=21reads); spawn50ms status polling but Busy can return the failed-unbound receipt rather than locally spin; durable retries1,2,4...300s. Existing pipe verification25ms/2s and bounded composer rereads exit on their first error. No new contention sleep or internal poller runs on Tokio workers. Request callers can arrive faster than these periodic schedules; one try_lock per attempted query is the bound, not an invented request-rate cap.

C33: a same-user indefinitely held lock is an accepted account-boundary residual, not an adversarial-hardening requirement. Its denial initially costs unavailable observations plus file/syscall/error/log work, later workload-dependent fallback launches; it does NOT silently erase panes or declare them dead. The fail-closed attach lock remains a BRAKE. The5s fallback is an existing answer/recovery contract, not a request to remove the brake or redesign tmux.

## Codex retry interaction — P280-002

The new expected Busy error reaches a preexisting one-look signal gate. A valid live pending spawned Codex row (proc=None, pane+spawn_id) is selected on first sight/thread-lock growth; bind_once stores the current lock snapshot and ALL pending IDs BEFORE bind_seat (:242-257). With valid child record/parent/singlethread facts, pane_pid (:301 ->143-148) can now return Busy Err. The error is logged only (:261-265); the row remains pending but seen. With unchanged row ID/lockset, every later5s tick filters it out (:253), even once contention is released. New lock, a row leaving/reentering pending, or a daemon restart are recovery signals; lock shrink/same-ID field update are not. Codex caller identity and SpawnWaits do not bind it, and paneless registration explicitly refuses a matching spawned pane row (registration.rs:1841-1844).

The Seen policy is preexisting and intentional for stable Ok(false) negative facts (codex_bind_tests.rs:192-219). The new transient Busy outcome is what exposes this interaction on otherwise-valid launch facts. Preserve the old stable-negative cost invariant if correcting it: transient UNKNOWN can be retried on an EXISTING next tick, not a new tight loop or per-seat always-on process probe. Independent correctness reviewer confirmed the source path; its one-shot pane-error receipt is included if available. No reproduction by this seat is claimed. The prime accepted this issue as F232 in the verdict header.

## Verification boundary

Read-only static/source/delta review and deterministic cost arithmetic by this seat; no builds, tests, samples, reloads or production contention injected. Author reports harness checks15/15 and20runs of held-process current-thread timer/zero-fork test, caught fork-on-contention and round1sleep mutants, crash sensor0/20with lock and20/20without. Source inspection confirms the new regression uses a separate holder PROCESS, checks an independent50ms timer (bounded tolerance), zero fixture tmux launches while skipped, and exactly one control launch after release. F228's CAS warmup correctly stays because skipped attach reads are not reservation outcomes. Test-only CLOEXEC allowance and S280-001 umask follow-up are not reopened.

Independent SAME-HEAD runtime receipt is now inspected (reviewer executed, not rerun by this seat):30 Busy list reads completed in4.039625ms with0forks; the primed50ms Tokio timer fired at53.234916ms. pane_process and kill returned Err, live-only variants returned None. After the HOLDER PROCESS was killed, the next read answered with exactly1control-client launch and0forks. This proves the short Busy window and acquisition-wait fix, not an indefinitely frozen holder's fallback rate. Receipt/diagnostic oracle confirms exact production head plus one isolated diagnostic test; machine-local paths are not published. The one-shot Codex binder-error runtime receipt is not yet available and is not asserted; F232 disposition rests on verified source and the prime's explicit acceptance. Deployment counters/CPU/RSS and20s machine spawn-rate remain gated on the prime's authorized deployment; separate same-identity windows, never subtract across a bounce.
